Before I paste it in: hypothermia is when your body loses heat faster than it can generate it, and it becomes life-threatening. It is analogous to losing weight in that it's all about using and losing energy... sort of the "flip side" of CICO.

tl/dr: "Starvation mode" is rare-but-real thing that only happens to people who are near death by starvation, and it is impossible for fatties to have it.

"Starvation mode" is a real thing, but it does NOT result in weight gain and it does not occur until one is actually starving to the point of being near death.

I'll use an analogy that won't elicit an emotional response: hypothermia. You get hypothermia from being in a cold environment when the outflow of body heat is greater than your body's ability to generate heat... it happens all the time, although deaths are fairly rare. Unless you've lived on the equator your entire life it has happened to you in at least a mild form. We've all been cold so we can all understand the basic principle, and we see the things the body does to combat hypothermia, like making you shiver (the movement generates heat). If the everyday things (like shivering or teeth chattering) don't reverse the heat loss the body recognizes the danger and will eventually take more drastic action. That drastic action is to "shut down" systems that aren't vital for your immediate survival on the grounds that, if your extremities get too cold you might lose a finger or two, but if your core temperature drops very much you'll die. Getting a little chilly might make you shiver, but it isn't going to make your body shut down "non-essential" functions to conserve heat: it wont do that unless your life is in imminent danger.

Likewise with "starvation mode:" while a starving person may experience bodily functions shutting down to prevent imminent death, that won't happen until the body's less-drastic measures have been exhausted. Obviously the primary way the body deals with an energy deficit is to deplete fat stores - that's why the body put them there in the first place when the person consumed the excess calories! For a person to go into "starvation mode" means that the body has so little energy available to it that it needs to immediately shut down "non-essential" systems to conserve what energy IS available to stave off imminent death. Anyone who's fat is not going to experience "starvation mode," because a fat body has lots of energy available in the form of fat deposits.

Obviously "starvation mode" will never cause weight gain in the absence of excess calorie consumption... no matter how hungry or malnourished you are, your body cannot create something from nothing. At worse, "starvation mode" is like end-stage hypothermia in that the body will reduce calorie usage by shutting down non-essential systems to prevent imminent death. It certainly won't make a fat person gain weight, nor will it prevent a fat person from losing weight while running a caloric deficit.
